I use PCP's. A tin of 500 .22 caliber pellets runs from about $7 to $16 which is a fair amount cheaper than rimfire ammunition. And yes, airguns are crazy quiet. That's why I went with the PCP's. Less moving parts equals less noise as well as an abundance of suppressor options. All you hear is the click of the action. The impact of the pellet makes more noise than the gun itself. There's considerably less recoil as well. Springers have a double recoil which destroys scopes that are built for anything less than a .50 BMG so take that into consideration. Optics can get expensive.

Pellet weight options for. 22 cal range from 14 grains to 34 grains. Slinging any of the medium to heavier weight pellets over 800 fps will give you more than enough energy at 50 yards to dispatch a gopher. However, if you feel that a .22 still isn't enough to meet your needs, there's larger pellet options. You can get pellets and cast slugs all the way up to .700 caliber. Most people feel that .25 cal is an excellent compromise as the heavier pellets buck the wind better and you only sacrifice just a touch of trajectory compared to a relatively flat shooting .22.

Yes, I was leaning towards a PCP myself in a .25. Primarily due to the extra energy and additional pellet options vs .30's.

Have you much experience with brands? Any to avoid completely? Conversely any of them stand head and shoulders above the rest?

That largely depends on your budget and what exactly you're looking for in a gun. Price reflects heavily on craftsmanship and more often than not, accuracy. Good barrels aren't cheap to produce.

As far as brands go, some need some work to reach their full potential. For instance, Hatsans are relatively affordable, powerful, and can go stealthy. They're also heavy and tend to have clunky actions and triggers. Nothing you can do about the weight but an experienced tuner such as Baxter Walton can smooth everything out for you and find your gun's pellet of choice. He'll actually build it to do whatever you want it to do. Accuracy, shot count, or power. Pick two.

For the money, I'd avoid KalibrGun. I've heard of too many issues for a gun in that price range. A good tune will fix any issues but shouldn't be necessary. Anything Daystate, FX, Taipan, or Vulcan are basically perfect out of the box. Little to nothing can be done to improve upon any of those brands. There's also several American manufacturers that are outstanding but lead time on production is pushed back for months. All of these guns are amazing and their prices reflect that. Rapid Air Weapons, American Air Arms, Scandalous Airguns, and Wicked Air Rifles all make incredible guns. WAR makes perhaps the stealthiest of the big bores.
